info.title: Mycelium Fabric — Functional Data Service API
info.summary: Platform data surrounding a SysML v2 model: organizations, projects, membership, ownership and reviews.
info.description:
The REST surface of the Mycelium Fabric Functional Data Service: the platform data
that surrounds a SysML v2 model, rather than the model itself. Projects, branches, commits and model
elements belong to the Concurrent Server and are reached through the OMG Systems Modelling API; a
reference held here to anything on that side is an identifier, never embedded content.

Generated from the Enterprise Architect model `SysML2_Software_Architecture.qea`, in which every
operation is a `«route»` on an `«apiModule»` class. Three conventions follow from that and are not
visible in the paths:

- **Authentication and authorization happen at the edge.** Every request passes an nginx
  `auth_request` subrequest to `/internal/auth`, which answers 200, 401 or 403 and stamps the
  resolved account onto the request it allows. No operation below declares 401 or 403, because the
  gate produces them for all of them uniformly, and no operation takes a current-user parameter.
- **A body never nests a composed child that has routes of its own.** A project body carries no
  members, ownerships, reviews or protection rules; each is created and deleted through its own
  path. The one exception is a project's policy, which has no routes and is therefore nested.
- **Server-assigned values are `readOnly`.** Identifiers and the audit stamps are omitted from
  request bodies and present in responses. A `PATCH` body is partial, so it is described by a
  separate `…Patch` schema with nothing required.

Collections are unpaged, deliberately: the expected volumes do not warrant it.

Operations carry `x-satisfies`, listing the Software System Specification requirements they
implement. Twelve of the forty-two have none, which is accurate rather than an omission: the
specification does not cover reviews or comments at all, and the gate, session and policy-read
operations are architectural.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: The nginx auth_request target, answering 200, 401 or 403 and stamping the resolved account onto the request it allows.

tags.name: Session
tags.description: The single call a client makes when it opens a session.

tags.name: Organizations
tags.description: The organization tree and its membership, including user creation since a user cannot exist outside an organization.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: The project and everything composed into it except reviews, which have their own module.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: The mirror of a Keycloak identity, which is readable here but owned there.

tags.name: Reviews
tags.description: Merge proposals on a project and the comment threads they carry.

parameters.name: X-Original-URI
parameters.description: The request being checked, forwarded by nginx because the auth subrequest carries neither the original uri nor its method.

parameters.name: X-Original-Method
parameters.description: The verb the action is inferred from; the auth subrequest itself is always a GET.

403.description: The account may not perform the action.

delete.description: Composition carries the delete down to the policy and to every project beneath.
Removing the last member is refused, because an organization is modelled as having at least one.

post.description: Scoped to an organization, because a user is modelled as belonging to at least one.
The requesting user becomes the project administrator, and the policy is created with the project.

get.description: Scoped by visibility, so a public project appears across organizations.

patch.description: Carries the lifecycle, the mode and the policy flags, so the handler authorises each field rather than the route.

delete.description: Composition carries the delete down to the policy, the members, the ownerships, the reviews and the protection rules.

put.description: The whole set is replaced, since nothing references a rule by identity.

requestBody.description: The complete rule set for the project.

patch.description: Transferring administration and reassigning an ownership are both changes to the membership.

delete.description: Refused while a member is still assigned to it.

post.description: Both branches live in the Concurrent Server, so only their identifiers are held here.

patch.description: Carries the status and the reviewer set, so submitting, approving and requesting changes are all status changes.

delete.description: Composition carries the delete down to every comment thread.

get.description: The thread is returned whole, since a reply and a quote each reference another comment.

post.description: A reply or a quote is a comment carrying the comment it answers.

patch.description: Resolving a comment is a status change.

delete.description: Composition carries the delete down to the replies.

patch.description: Limited to the preferences and the platform status, because Keycloak owns the name, the mail and the identifier.

get.description: The projects the user is a member of, which is narrower than what visibility would let them open.

bearerAuth.description: An access token issued by the identity provider the deployment is configured against. The gate validates it; no service below sees a credential.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with a constraint of the data model.
